Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of 
${\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-2,3)$ and the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [3,5].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,3).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =b\cdot h \\  & =5\cdot 2 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot (1)^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =10+\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
